sets.title: Editing · four Primary 3 passages
sets.instruction: Each line has one spelling or grammar error. Write the correction — one word only. This is the Booklet B section worth ten marks, so work line by line and do not rush.

questions.q: Passage A — The Hamster That Got Out — Our class hamster is call Pepper.
questions.tip: The error was “call”. It needs “is called”, not “is call”.

questions.q: Passage A — The Hamster That Got Out — He live in a cage beside the window.
questions.tip: The error was “live”. “He” is singular, so the verb takes an -s.

questions.q: Passage A — The Hamster That Got Out — Last Friday somebody forget to close the little door.
questions.tip: The error was “forget”. The past tense of “forget” is “forgot”.

questions.q: Passage A — The Hamster That Got Out — On Monday morning the cage was empty and we could not find him nowhere.
questions.tip: The error was “nowhere”. Two negatives cancel out; use “anywhere” after “not”.

questions.q: Passage A — The Hamster That Got Out — Mrs Tan told us to look under the cupboardes.
questions.tip: The error was “cupboardes”. “Cupboard” just adds -s.

questions.q: Passage A — The Hamster That Got Out — Suresh find him behind the recycling box.
questions.tip: The error was “find”. The rest of the story is in the past.

questions.q: Passage A — The Hamster That Got Out — Pepper had eat a whole packet of sunflower seeds.
questions.tip: The error was “eat”. After “had” we use “eaten”.

questions.q: Passage A — The Hamster That Got Out — He was to fat to climb back into the cage by himself.
questions.tip: The error was “to”. “Too fat” means more fat than it should be.

questions.q: Passage A — The Hamster That Got Out — We putted him back and shut the door properly.
questions.tip: The error was “putted”. The past tense of “put” is “put”.

questions.q: Passage A — The Hamster That Got Out — Now two pupils check the door every day before they goes home.
questions.tip: The error was “goes”. “They” does not take an -s on the verb.

questions.q: Passage B — The School Fun Fair — Our school hold a fun fair every October.
questions.tip: The error was “hold”. “Our school” is singular, so the verb takes an -s.

questions.q: Passage B — The School Fun Fair — Last year it were held on a Saturday morning.
questions.tip: The error was “were”. “It” takes “was”.

questions.q: Passage B — The School Fun Fair — Each class had they own stall.
questions.tip: The error was “they”. “Their” shows that the stalls belonged to them.

questions.q: Passage B — The School Fun Fair — My class sold sandwichs and iced barley water.
questions.tip: The error was “sandwichs”. Words ending in -ch add -es.

questions.q: Passage B — The School Fun Fair — We charged a dollar for a sandwich and fifty cent for a drink.
questions.tip: The error was “cent”. Fifty is more than one, so the noun is plural.

questions.q: Passage B — The School Fun Fair — A long queue form before we had even finished setting up.
questions.tip: The error was “form”. The story is in the past.

questions.q: Passage B — The School Fun Fair — By ten o'clock we had sell everything.
questions.tip: The error was “sell”. After “had” we use “sold”.

questions.q: Passage B — The School Fun Fair — The money goed to the school's library fund.
questions.tip: The error was “goed”. The past tense of “go” is “went”.

questions.q: Passage B — The School Fun Fair — Mr Siva said it was a excellent effort.
questions.tip: The error was “a”. “Excellent” begins with a vowel sound, so it takes “an”.

questions.q: Passage B — The School Fun Fair — This year we are planning a even bigger stall.
questions.tip: The error was “a”. “Even” begins with a vowel sound.

questions.q: Passage C — The Thunderstorm — The sky turn dark just before we were dismissed.
questions.tip: The error was “turn”. The rest of the sentence is in the past.

questions.q: Passage C — The Thunderstorm — Mrs Devi tell us to wait inside the hall.
questions.tip: The error was “tell”. The past tense of “tell” is “told”.

questions.q: Passage C — The Thunderstorm — There was already more than fifty pupil in there.
questions.tip: The error was “pupil”. Fifty is more than one, so the noun is plural.

questions.q: Passage C — The Thunderstorm — The rain come down so hard that we could not hear the announcement.
questions.tip: The error was “come”. The past tense of “come” is “came”.

questions.q: Passage C — The Thunderstorm — Hui Ling and me sat on the floor near the stage.
questions.tip: The error was “me”. It is part of the subject: “Hui Ling and I sat”.

questions.q: Passage C — The Thunderstorm — She had bringed an umbrella but it was in her locker.
questions.tip: The error was “bringed”. The past tense of “bring” is “brought”.

questions.q: Passage C — The Thunderstorm — My shoes was wet right through.
questions.tip: The error was “was”. “Shoes” is plural, so it takes “were”.

questions.q: Passage C — The Thunderstorm — After half a hour the rain stopped.
questions.tip: The error was “a”. “Hour” begins with a vowel sound because the h is silent.

questions.q: Passage C — The Thunderstorm — The sun came out and the puddles begun to shrink.
questions.tip: The error was “begun”. Without “had”, the past tense is “began”.

questions.q: Passage C — The Thunderstorm — We walked home slowly, jumping over every puddles on the way.
questions.tip: The error was “puddles”. “Every” is followed by a singular noun.

questions.q: Passage D — Grandmother's Garden — My grandmother grow chillies on her corridor.
questions.tip: The error was “grow”. “My grandmother” is singular, so the verb takes an -s.

questions.q: Passage D — Grandmother's Garden — She have eleven pots altogether.
questions.tip: The error was “have”. “She” takes “has”.

questions.q: Passage D — Grandmother's Garden — The biggest pot is tallest than me.
questions.tip: The error was “tallest”. Comparing two things takes “taller than”; “tallest” is for three or more.

questions.q: Passage D — Grandmother's Garden — Every morning she water them before the sun gets hot.
questions.tip: The error was “water”. “She” is singular, so the verb takes an -s.

questions.q: Passage D — Grandmother's Garden — Last month two of the plant died.
questions.tip: The error was “plant”. “Two of the” is followed by a plural noun.

questions.q: Passage D — Grandmother's Garden — She digged them up and put in new soil.
questions.tip: The error was “digged”. The past tense of “dig” is “dug”.

questions.q: Passage D — Grandmother's Garden — Now there are more leafs than before.
questions.tip: The error was “leafs”. The plural of “leaf” is “leaves”.

questions.q: Passage D — Grandmother's Garden — She give the chillies to our neighbours because she cannot eat them all.
questions.tip: The error was “give”. “She” is singular, so the verb takes an -s.

questions.q: Passage D — Grandmother's Garden — Yesterday she teached me how to take a cutting.
questions.tip: The error was “teached”. The past tense of “teach” is “taught”.

questions.q: Passage D — Grandmother's Garden — I am going to try grow one in my own room.
questions.tip: The error was “grow”. After “try” we use the -ing form here: “try growing”.

sets.title: Punctuation · 30 sentences to rewrite
sets.instruction: Rewrite each line with capital letters and punctuation put right. Write it out in full, then compare it with the answer and mark yourself.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: my birthday is on the 3rd of june
questions.m: My birthday is on the 3rd of June
questions.tip: Capital letter at the start, and June is the name of a month.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: where is my reading book
questions.tip: A question needs a question mark.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: we went to the zoo on tuesday
questions.m: We went to the zoo on Tuesday
questions.tip: Days of the week always start with a capital letter.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: i live in singapore with my mother father and sister
questions.m: I live in Singapore with my mother, father and sister
questions.tip: 'I' is always a capital. Singapore is a place name. Commas separate items in a list.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: what a loud noise that was
questions.m: What a loud noise that was!
questions.tip: A 'what a…' sentence that shows surprise takes an exclamation mark.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: mrs lim teaches us english and mathematics
questions.m: Mrs Lim teaches us English and Mathematics
questions.tip: A person's title and name take capitals, and so do the names of subjects that are languages or proper nouns.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: the cat is sleeping the dog is awake
questions.m: The cat is sleeping. The dog is awake.
questions.tip: These are two separate sentences, so they need a full stop between them.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: can you help me carry this box
questions.m: Can you help me carry this box?
questions.tip: A question needs a question mark.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: hari said i am ready
questions.tip: A comma after 'said', then inverted commas round the words that were spoken.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: we bought apples oranges pears and bananas
questions.m: We bought apples, oranges, pears and bananas
questions.tip: Commas between the items, but not before the final 'and'.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: dont forget your water bottle
questions.tip: 'Don't' is short for 'do not', so it needs an apostrophe.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: the boys bags are in the corridor
questions.m: The boys' bags are in the corridor
questions.tip: The bags belong to more than one boy, so the apostrophe goes after the s.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: my sisters name is nadia
questions.tip: One sister owns the name, so the apostrophe comes before the s. Nadia is a name.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: stop shouted the teacher
questions.tip: A shout takes an exclamation mark, inside the inverted commas.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: is this your pencil case asked mei
questions.m: "Is this your pencil case?" asked Mei
questions.tip: The question mark goes inside the inverted commas, and Mei is a name.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: on monday we have pe on friday we have art
questions.m: On Monday we have PE. On Friday we have Art.
questions.tip: Two sentences, so a full stop between them. Days and subjects take capitals.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: i cant come because im not well
questions.m: I can't come because I'm not well
questions.tip: Both 'can't' and 'I'm' are shortened, so both need an apostrophe.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: the river nile is in africa
questions.m: The River Nile is in Africa
questions.tip: The names of rivers and continents take capital letters.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: how many brothers do you have
questions.m: How many brothers do you have?
questions.tip: A question needs a question mark.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: ravi likes football tennis and swimming
questions.m: Ravi likes football, tennis and swimming
questions.tip: Commas between the items in the list, and a capital for Ravi.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: we are going to malaysia in december
questions.m: We are going to Malaysia in December
questions.tip: Countries and months take capital letters.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: look out the branch is falling
questions.m: Look out! The branch is falling.
questions.tip: A warning takes an exclamation mark, and then a new sentence begins.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: the childrens playground is behind block b
questions.m: The children's playground is behind Block B
questions.tip: 'Children' is already plural, so the apostrophe comes before the s.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: mother asked have you finished your homework
questions.m: Mother asked, "Have you finished your homework?"
questions.tip: A comma after 'asked', inverted commas round the question, and the question mark inside them.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: that isnt mine said suresh
questions.tip: An apostrophe in 'isn't', a comma before 'said', and a capital for Suresh.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: we visited the science centre the bird park and the museum
questions.m: We visited the Science Centre, the Bird Park and the Museum
questions.tip: Commas between the items, and capital letters because these are the names of particular places.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: my fathers car is red my uncles car is blue
questions.m: My father's car is red. My uncle's car is blue.
questions.tip: One father and one uncle, so the apostrophe comes before the s in each. Two sentences, so a full stop between them.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: why is the gate locked asked the boy
questions.m: "Why is the gate locked?" asked the boy
questions.tip: The question mark belongs inside the inverted commas, because the boy asked the question.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: hurry up well be late
questions.tip: An exclamation mark after the order, then a new sentence. 'We'll' is short for 'we will'.

questions.q: Rewrite with correct punctuation: in january we move to a new classroom
questions.m: In January we move to a new classroom
questions.tip: A capital at the start of the sentence and a capital for the month.

sets.title: Spelling · 40 words to get right
sets.instruction: Each word below is spelt wrongly. Write it correctly.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: becuase
questions.tip: It is be-CAUSE: the cause comes after the be.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: freind
questions.tip: Remember: a friend to the end — f-r-i-e-n-d.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: alot
questions.tip: 'A lot' is always two words.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: thier
questions.tip: Their follows the same i-before-e rule as 'friend': t-h-e-i-r.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: wich
questions.tip: Which begins with wh-, like what, when and where.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: recieve
questions.tip: After a c, it is e before i: receive.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: tomorow
questions.tip: Tomorrow has one m and two r's.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: beatiful
questions.tip: Beautiful keeps the whole word 'beauty' at the start: beauti-ful.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: intresting
questions.tip: Say it in four parts: in-ter-est-ing.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: diffrent
questions.tip: Say it in three parts: dif-fer-ent.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: favourate
questions.tip: It ends -ite, like 'bite': favour-ite.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: libary
questions.tip: There are two r's: li-brar-y.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: Febuary
questions.tip: There is an r after the b: Feb-ru-ary.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: excercise
questions.tip: Only one c, and it comes after the x: ex-er-cise.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: resturant
questions.tip: There is an a after the t: rest-au-rant.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: vegtable
questions.tip: There is an e in the middle: veg-e-table.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: choclate
questions.tip: Three parts: choc-o-late.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: brocolli
questions.tip: Two c's and two l's: broc-co-li.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: surprize
questions.tip: It ends in -ise, and there is an r after the su.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: definately
questions.tip: It has 'finite' in the middle: de-finite-ly.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: seperate
questions.tip: There is 'a rat' in the middle: sep-a-rate.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: embarassed
questions.tip: Two r's and two s's: em-bar-rassed.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: neccessary
questions.tip: One c and two s's: nec-es-sary.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: begining
questions.tip: Double the n before -ing: be-gin-ning.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: writting
questions.tip: One t in writing, two in written.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: stoped
questions.tip: Double the p before -ed: stopped.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: planed
questions.tip: Double the n before -ed: planned.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: happend
questions.tip: There is an e before the n: happ-ened.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: untill
questions.tip: Until has only one l at the end.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: allready
questions.tip: 'Already' has one l.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: alright
questions.tip: Write it as two words: all right.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: goverment
questions.tip: There is an n before the m: govern-ment.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: enviroment
questions.tip: There is an n before the m: environ-ment.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: quite
questions.tip: Quiet means silent and has two syllables: qui-et. 'Quite' means fairly.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: woudl
questions.tip: Would rhymes with could and should: w-o-u-l-d.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: becomming
questions.tip: One m in becoming.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: usualy
questions.tip: Two l's: usual + ly.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: finaly
questions.tip: Two l's: final + ly.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: carefull
questions.tip: The suffix -ful has only one l.

questions.q: Spell this word correctly: sucessful
questions.tip: Two c's and two s's in the middle: suc-cess-ful.
